transcript:
Header:
Date: 2028-05-09
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Daniel Kim (CTO - NovaSearch), Rosa Martinez (Head of Search), Liam O'Connell (Engineer)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Redwood did a hosted API demo focusing on embeddings + reranking for search relevance. Walked through candidate generation -> embeddings store -> reranker call flow, discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, storage options (FAISS vs managed), and security concerns (SOC2, SSO, KMS). Agreed to provision trial API key and run benchmarks on NovaSearch query set; Redwood to send pricing and security docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Okay hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, and with me is Priya Shah our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:04] Daniel Kim: Hey thanks, doing good. We were excited to see the embeddings + rerank flow, we've been evaluating a few options.
[00:10] Rosa Martinez: Yeah hi, Rosa here. We're particularly interested in improving query relevance for long-tail queries.
[00:15] Priya Shah: Great. Quick agenda: we'll show the hosted API endpoints for embeddings and rerank, demo the Console for observability and Optimize suggestions, and then go over security and next steps.
[00:23] Liam O'Connell: Cool. Our current stack is Elastic 8.x with a custom learning-to-rank model run offline. We store vectors in FAISS on a separate service. Latency and maintenance are a pain.
[00:33] Alex Morgan: Thanks, that helps. We'll show how Redwood can be used as a managed embeddings store + on-the-fly reranker to replace the offline LTR path, and what the latency / cost looks like.
[00:42] Priya Shah: Jumping in — here's the call flow: candidate generation (Elastic or naive filtering) -> call Redwood embeddings endpoint to vectorize docs and query -> nearest neighbour search in your vector index (we demo using FAISS locally) -> send top-K candidates to Redwood rerank endpoint which runs a cross-encoder style re-ranker.
[00:59] [00:59] Priya Shah: (mumbling) excuse the demo noise, switching screens — ok can you all see the Console?
[01:05] Daniel Kim: Yes we can. The Console UI looks familiar.
[01:08] Priya Shah: Good. On the left is Models, here's our embeddings models, you can pick dimension size and variant — for example "emb-small-384" vs "emb-compact-1024" — there's tradeoffs, smaller dims are faster and cheaper but may lose nuance on long-tail language.
[01:26] Rosa Martinez: How do you recommend picking dimension size? We have a lot of short product queries and some long customer support queries.
[01:32] Priya Shah: For mixed workloads we often recommend a 768- or 1024-d model for recall and then a reranker to push precision. Optimize will suggest quantization and batching profiles based on your token lengths and qps.
[01:44] Liam O'Connell: Do you host the vectors or do we keep them? We prefer vectors in our VPC currently.
[01:50] Alex Morgan: Hosted option stores vectors in Redwood's managed store, but we also support VPC/private deployments for vectors and an option to push embeddings to your FAISS cluster. For this pilot most customers start hosted for velocity, then move to Dedicated/VPC if they need isolation.
[02:05] Daniel Kim: Latency numbers? We're aiming 100ms median for search return.
[02:10] Priya Shah: For the typical flow — embed query (~15-40ms), kNN search depends on index and K (~5-50ms), rerank cross-encoder call can be 50-120ms depending on model size. With smaller reranker variants we can target 60-90ms, and batching helps reduce cost if you can tolerate slightly higher p95. Our Console shows per-route breakdowns.
[02:32] [02:32] Alex Morgan: Quick note — those reranker times are for hosted GPUs; if you need sub-50ms p50 at scale we recommend a Dedicated pool with pinned capacity.
[02:42] Rosa Martinez: What's the cost delta on reranker vs just doing vector-only?
[02:46] Priya Shah: Rerank adds compute cost, roughly 2-4x per-request depending on model size. But it often reduces downstream user friction and search sessions, so cost per successful query can be lower. Optimize can estimate unit economics from a sample trace.
[03:01] Liam O'Connell: Our main concern is data residency and compliance; we need SOC2 and SSO.
[03:06] Alex Morgan: We are SOC 2 Type II and support SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS-based encryption for Private deployments. We'll share the security whitepaper and SOC2 report after the call.
[03:18] [03:18] Daniel Kim: Great, please share that. Also curious on what model variants you recommend for our dataset.
[03:24] Priya Shah: For NovaSearch we suggest starting with emb-768 plus a medium reranker — it balances cost and precision. If recall is critical we bump to emb-1024. We also showed in the Console how you can run an A/B rollout to measure quality change against a holdout.
[03:40] [03:40] Priya Shah: Switching to a live example — here's a sample product query "best headphones under $200 for travel". We vectorize the query, show nearest neighbors, then call the reranker to re-score the top 50 candidates.
[03:54] [03:54] Priya Shah: (demo) Note the reranker pushes up documents that mention "noise cancellation" and "lightweight" even if they were lower in lexical score. The confidence scores are in the JSON response.
[04:10] Rosa Martinez: That looks promising. How are you measuring user-perceived relevance in Console?
[04:14] Priya Shah: We have a Quality dashboard — you can upload labelled queries/expected docs and compute precision@k and MRR over time. We also trigger regression alerts tied to evaluation sets.
[04:26] Daniel Kim: For storage, if we keep vectors in our FAISS, what does integration look like?
[04:31] Priya Shah: Two options: 1) push embeddings via API to your FAISS and use Redwood only for inference (rerank + embed) — you host retrieval; 2) use Redwood managed vector store and call a single rerank endpoint; we provide sync tools to keep vectors in sync. Option 1 is common for customers with strict residency.
[04:50] Liam O'Connell: If we do option 1, do you support approximate indexes like HNSW and the tuning knobs?
[04:55] Priya Shah: Yes, we support HNSW/IVF configs on the FAISS side; the main difference is how you tune ef/search_k and recall targets. We'll share recommended config defaults.
[05:06] [05:06] Alex Morgan: Quick plug — Optimize will analyze your query length distribution and suggest batch sizes and quantization to lower costs without hurting quality. You can preview cost delta in Console.
[05:18] Daniel Kim: Can we see logs/traces for a single query path?
[05:21] Priya Shah: Absolutely — trace view shows per-token timing and per-service hop; here's an example trace that shows embed->knn->rerank and token-level latencies.
[05:33] [05:33] (minor crosstalk)
[05:35] Rosa Martinez: Any gotchas migrating from our current offline LTR?
[05:38] Priya Shah: Two things: you need a labeled relevance set to validate the reranker, and you should monitor for regressions during rollout. Also pay attention to cold-start docs — using a hybrid approach (bm25 + embeddings) helps.
[05:52] Liam O'Connell: What about rate limits and quotas on hosted?
[05:56] Alex Morgan: Hosted has soft rate limits per account; for production traffic we recommend Dedicated with reserved capacity. Hosted is great for pilot and early traffic.
[06:06] Daniel Kim: For the pilot, how long to get a test key and start benchmarking?
[06:09] Alex Morgan: We can provision a trial API key today — Priya will follow up with instructions and a sample dataset ingest script.
[06:16] Priya Shah: I'll also share a benchmark harness (Python script) that runs your query set through embeddings+rerank and reports p50/p95 and cost estimates.
[06:25] [06:25] Daniel Kim: Ok good. Also one more question: can reranker be constrained to return explainability signals or token highlights for why a doc was promoted?
[06:34] Priya Shah: We provide feature attributions at a high level — token highlights may be noisy from cross-encoders but we can return top contributing spans and scores. It's in beta and we can enable it for you in the pilot.
[06:48] Rosa Martinez: About pricing model — is rerank priced per token or per inference?
[06:53] Alex Morgan: Embeddings are per-vector call and per-dimension tier; rerank is priced per-inference (model size buckets) and we show a cost breakdown in Console. We'll include detailed pricing tiers in the follow-up.
[07:05] Daniel Kim: Sounds good. Any competitors you think we should be aware of if we go hosted?
[07:09] Alex Morgan: Common ones are Algolia for integrated search and Elastic/OpenSearch for self-hosting; for managed vector APIs some customers consider specialized vendors. We'll include a brief competitive note.
[07:20] [07:20] Alex Morgan: Ok time to recap and next steps — we heard NovaSearch wants to improve long-tail relevance, target ~100ms median, need SOC2/SSO, and prefer to pilot hosted and possibly keep vectors in-house. Next steps: provisioning trial key + sample dataset, sharing security docs, sending pricing/SLA, and scheduling a POC scoping call.
[07:42] Daniel Kim: Perfect. We'll upload a sample of query logs and a labelled set for evaluation.
[07:47] Liam O'Connell: I'll put the dataset in the shared S3 link you send.
[07:51] Rosa Martinez: Thanks, this was helpful.
[07:54] Alex Morgan: Thanks everyone, Priya and I will follow up with the items.
[07:58] (meeting ends)
